speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesenteric Ischemia

The combination of sudden onset periumbilical pain, bloody stools, and a recent acute myocardial infarction in a 74-year-old male is highly suggestive of mesenteric ischemia, likely due to thromboembolism. While the CT scan was reportedly negative, this can occur in early ischemia before bowel wall necrosis or pneumatosis develops. Given the severity of the symptoms and the high mortality risk, we must proceed with an emergent diagnostic laparotomy to assess bowel viability.
